newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower on electricity sector.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower on electricity sector.

text.p: A wave of selling by foreign investors of Chilean electricity shares dragged down blue chips at the close, said dealers.
The bolsa could open firm, but the underlying mood will remain cautious until a battle between the government and power companies over electricity rates is resolved, they said.
"The uncertainty surrounding the recent conflicts in the power sector has gone down badly abroad," said one trader.
The selective IPSA index ended off 0.72 percent at 97.14 points. The general IGPA index lost 0.45 percent at 5,280.79 points in volume of 9.8 billion pesos.
Traders said most of the local dealing was by brokers trading their own portfolios with institutional investors staying clear of the market.
Investors' confidence in the electricity sector has been undermined by delays in a court ruling over an appeal by utility Chilectra against government plans to cut distribution rates, said dealers.
The court has postponed the case until next week. The new prices were due to have come into force on November 4.
Power shares have also been undermined by fears that a serious drought in central Chile will hurt generating company earnings, they said.
Losers included utility Edelnor, down 3.03 percent at 320 pesos, and steel-maker Cap, which lost 2.73 percent at 1,070 pesos.
Winners included forestry firm Masisa, up 1.78 percent at 200 pesos, pasta producer Lucchetti, up 1.74 percent at 117 pesos, and salmon company Mainstream which rose 1.51 percent to 33 pesos.
